reviews.quote: With the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 options the new ROG Zephyrus G14 is currently pretty unrivaled. Very high-quality and compact aluminum case, brilliant OLED display at 120 Hz with G-Sync, excellent speakers, great input devices. Cons: soldered-on RAM, PWM flickering, limited maximum HDR brightness, loud fans. (NBC review of the GA403WW RTX 5080 config, "top rated" award.)

professional.note: No pro review of the 2026 GU405 retrieved (hard-stop, disclosed). Anchored on the 2025 GA403 line via SHARED-zephyrus-g14.md.

praises: RTX 5070 Ti 12GB in a ~1.5kg 14" chassis: the strongest thin-and-light gaming option at Best Buy CA, DLSS4 frame-gen shines at 3K
12GB VRAM is meaningfully better for AI/local-LLC work than the 8GB 5060/5070 tiers
Same class-leading 3K OLED 120Hz panel and premium aluminum build as the rest of the G14 line
Current on sale $500 off ($4,299) — best G14 spec-per-dollar moment of the line
Still USB-C chargeable and travel-sized despite the top-tier GPU
complaints: At $4,799 regular this is thin-and-light-tax pricing; thicker laptops (Strix/Legion) give a 5080 for similar money
5070 Ti in a 1.5kg chassis is heavily TGP-capped and thermally throttled under sustained AAA loads; expect hot deck + loud Turbo fan
Soldered RAM (32GB only), single M.2 — zero upgrade headroom at flagship price
2026 GU405 is brand-new: no long-term reliability track record yet, and BBY listing has zero reviews today
Battery drains fastest of the G14 line under load (biggest GPU + Arrow Lake-H on 73Wh)

design_philosophy: The 2026 GU405 pushes ASUS's halo 14" into true enthusiast territory: an Intel Arrow Lake Ultra 9 paired with a 12GB RTX 5070 Ti in the same aluminum OLED ultrabook-weight chassis. It embodies the line's bet that gamers will trade raw TGP and upgradability for portability and screen quality — accepting that the GPU runs below its rated watts to keep 1.5kg. This is the performance flagship of the CA G14 range.
